results.detail: Reviewed CAS migration applied to disposable PostgreSQL database.
service_role can execute; anon/authenticated cannot execute.
SystemConfigs has RLS; service_role has required table privileges; anon/authenticated do not.
A valid non-partial single-column unique index protects SystemConfigs.key.
JSONB expected value with reordered object keys matched atomically.
Stale expected JSON returned zero rows without changing current value.
JSON null does not match the current object and preserves its value; SQL CAS compares JSONB values, while API revision validation is a separate contract.
anon/authenticated receive permission denied for the writer RPC.
Two independent PostgreSQL transactions from one snapshot produced exactly one success and one conflict.
Rollback restored the exact fixture value; second rollback was a zero-row no-op.
Rollback conflict preserved an intervening unrelated edit.
Absent-row insert succeeded once; rerun with absent expectation returned conflict.

residual: This runner proves the CAS RPC/fixture DB behavior only.
Migration storage failure injection, crash/restart/resume and durable backup restore require a separate storage adapter/fixture and remain NOT VERIFIED here.
No production database, Storage bucket, or remote Supabase project was contacted.
